title: OpenTelemetry GenAI — Tracing Tool Calls End-to-End
service: GenAITrace: OTel GenAI spans for a tool-calling agent with a scripted model and MCP server; a trace linker, an OTLP/JSON span log, semconv checks and GenAI histograms, traceparent propagation over stdio and HTTP with batched OTLP/JSON export, and self time with the heaviest chain

parts.lesson_anchor: Span hierarchy (one trace id for agent -> LLM -> tool -> MCP); Span kinds (CLIENT across a process boundary, INTERNAL for the agent's own steps); Opt-in content capture; code/main.py start_span, fake_mcp_call, fake_llm_call; Use It: 'Trace id is shared across all spans. Parent-child links are encoded via parentSpanId.'
planted_bugs: Tracer.start_span mints a new trace id even when it has a parent; the failure surfaces in traces.link, which splits one run into 9 traces (assert 9 == 1)
fake_mcp_call starts mcp.call as INTERNAL, although its docstring and the lesson make a call into the MCP server CLIENT

content_capture_enabled returns env.get('OTEL_CAPTURE_CONTENT') != '0', so an unset variable (None) turns capture on and prompts, completions and tool arguments land in span events by default; the events are added in fake_llm_call and fake_tool_execute, the root cause is the helper Tracer.__init__ calls
traces.link scans every span to find each parent, O(n^2)
parts.timing_assert: link() on a 6,500-tool-call session (13,003 spans) under 0.12 s; the linear scan takes 1.05-2.4 s on this machine depending on load, the (trace id, span id) index 5-13 ms
parts.overfix_guard: a span whose parent is not among the spans (a sub-agent's root, its parent in the calling process) stays in its trace as a root and keeps parent_span_id: an index lookup that raises, a continue that drops it, and clearing the id are caught; the index is keyed by trace id too (a parent span id that equals another trace's root, and replayed spans with the same span ids under another trace id); every run without a parent starts its own trace; only OTEL_CAPTURE_CONTENT=1 turns capture on ('0' and 'true' do not) and =1 does; tool.execute stays INTERNAL; traces come in the order their first span appears (sorting by trace id before grouping is caught)
parts.deviation: The suggested exporter-side parent lookup sits in the trace linker (traces.link), which Part 5 builds on; OTLP export needs no parent lookup. The remote mark is the parent_span_id the root keeps: the lesson names no OTLP field for it. The timing case is 13,003 spans instead of 20,000, so that the quadratic version stays near 1-2 s. Span.to_otlp moved to Part 2, where the value encoding and its precision traps belong.

parts.lesson_anchor: Exporters: OTLP as the wire; the OTLP/JSON shape the quiz (Q9) and the code walkthrough describe (attributes as key/value lists, kind as an enum); Events on spans
parts.exactness: spans read back field for field across two reopens: nanosecond timestamps far above 2**53 (start, end and event times), 32- and 16-character lowercase hex ids, int vs float vs bool attribute types, int64 bounds, arrays of each scalar type and the empty array, two events with the same name in order; the raw file is also read with json.loads(parse_int=float), the way JavaScript or jq would, and timestamps and 2**53 + 1 must survive it
traps: 64-bit integers written as JSON numbers (timestamps, event times, intValue)
loosening the given strict reader instead of fixing the writer
isinstance(True, int): True written as an intValue
1.0 written as an intValue
no int64 range check, or an off-by-one range
bool and int, or int and float, mixed in one array; checking items only against the first item's type
nested lists, None and dicts accepted
events keyed by name
the log opened with 'w'; a new log raising FileNotFoundError
an unfinished span written; a root's parentSpanId written as null; the kind written as its name
parts.deviation: The candidate writes encode_value, to_otlp and SpanLog; the reader (from_otlp, decode_value) is given and strict. The 64-bit-as-decimal-string rule is stated in the otlp.py docstring with its reason (readers whose numbers are doubles). Torn lines, flush and U+2028 traps are left out: 13/01's session log has them.

parts.lesson_anchor: Required attributes (LLM, tool and agent spans); Span kinds; Opt-in content capture; Metrics (gen_ai.client.token.usage, gen_ai.client.operation.duration, gen_ai.tool.execution.duration); quiz Q11 bucket bounds
traps: 0 tokens counted as missing; an empty string counted as present
response.model differing from request.model reported
execute_tool allowed only as INTERNAL (the agent's own mcp.call is execute_tool and CLIENT)
spans without gen_ai.operation.name checked; an unknown operation not reported, or checked further (KeyError)
a span's problems out of order: kind first, then missing attributes in REQUIRED order
scrub dropping every event, editing the spans it is given, or dropping content with capture on
a value on a bound put in the next bucket (bisect_right, <); no slot above the last bound
input and output tokens merged; 0 tokens not recorded; a missing token count raising; token samples taken only from spans that have both counts (a cut-off stream has input tokens only)
chat and tool spans picked by span name instead of gen_ai.operation.name and kind
the MCP round trip (CLIENT execute_tool) counted as a second tool call
tool durations keyed by call id; chat durations keyed by the served model
durations scaled with * 1e-9: 75 ms becomes 0.07500000000000001 and crosses the 0.075 bound
parts.integration: the agent run from Part 1 (with content capture on) must pass check() with no problems and gives the gpt-4o and get_weather samples
clarifying_questions: metrics for spans that failed the checks
parts.deviation: execute_tool spans may be INTERNAL or CLIENT, because the lesson's own mcp.call span is execute_tool and CLIENT. gen_ai.tool.execution.duration counts only the INTERNAL span of each tool call. The lesson gives no required attributes for text_completion or embeddings, so the checker has rules for the three operations the agent emits and reports any other value as an unknown operation. Dimensions: token usage by token type, operation duration by request model, tool duration by tool name. The bucket rule (a value on a bound belongs to the bucket it closes) is in the Histogram docstring; the duration bounds are quiz Q11's.

parts.lesson_anchor: Propagation across MCP (traceparent header over Streamable HTTP, _meta.traceparent over stdio); Exercise 4; quiz Q3 and Q10 (traceparent layout, all-zero ids invalid, a bad traceparent starts a new trace); Exporters (OTLP); the walkthrough's batch span processor
parts.wire_format: one OTLP/JSON export request per batch, as UTF-8 bytes: resourceSpans -> scopeSpans -> spans, service.name as an OTLP attribute, spans as Part 2's to_otlp, decided by the test's json.loads and unpack()
traps: upper-case hex, other versions, wrong lengths, extra fields and all-zero ids accepted
re.match with ^...$ (the quiz's pattern) accepts a trailing newline; match instead of fullmatch
int(x, 16) accepts upper case, 0x, + and underscores (flags too: 0A)
a non-string traceparent raising TypeError; a malformed one raising instead of starting a new trace
inject dropping other _meta keys, changing the caller's request (shallow copy), writing the body over HTTP, or a header over stdio
the agent not injecting, or injecting the tool span instead of the mcp.call span
a full batch not sent from the on_end that fills it (only on tick, > instead of >=, one request per span)
tick with > instead of >=; the wait counted from the last request, from the newest span, or from the span's own end_ns instead of the on_end call; tick on an empty queue raising
shutdown not flushing; spans that end after shutdown queued, or raising
requests as str; resource attributes as a plain object; one resourceSpans per span; a batch sorted by start time
clarifying_questions: failing the request on a bad traceparent
parts.deviation: 'Unfinished spans are not exported' follows from the on_end design: spans reach the exporter only when they end, and a span still running at shutdown is dropped when it ends; the test checks both. 'In end order within a batch' holds by construction and is checked by decoding every request. The time trigger is an explicit tick() on the exporter's clock instead of a timer thread, so the test needs no real time. Wiring inject into the agent's fake_mcp_call (Exercise 4) is part of this part.

parts.lesson_anchor: The Problem (sometimes 30 s: an MCP server's cold start); Span hierarchy; the span waterfall figure; the walkthrough's waterfall (a parent's duration contains its children)
traps: child durations summed instead of the union of their intervals (parallel tools)
intervals merged in the order given (link keeps the end order a collector delivers)
covered time taken as first start to last end (a 50 ms gap between children)
children not clipped, or clipped at one end only (a SERVER span that ends after, and one that starts before, its mcp.call)
a child entirely outside its parent subtracting a negative length
self times only for spans with children
the chain following the child with the most self time, or the longest child, or weighing a subtree by its heaviest span instead of the sum
ties not going to the smaller span id
weights memoized by span name
the chain stopping one level down
parts.deviation: The critical path is defined as the heaviest self-time chain from a root to a leaf, ties to the smaller span id. Part 5 uses Part 1's link, which already makes a span whose parent never arrived a root of its own, so that case is checked here as a chain of its own rather than as a separate tree-building trap.

deviations: Part 1's parent lookup is in the trace linker rather than the OTLP exporter, and Span.to_otlp moved to Part 2 (see the Part 1 and Part 2 notes).

Part 4 keeps the suggested traps that a push-based exporter can still get wrong (a full batch sent at once, end order, a malformed traceparent starting a new trace); 'unfinished spans are not exported' is checked through a span that ends after shutdown.
Part 3's checker has rules only for chat, execute_tool and invoke_agent, the operations the lesson's agent emits.
